title: Is the Future of Medicine Hidden in Ancient DNA?

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 嘿，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在黑胶唱片时代的夜店里做 DJ 的时候，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每晚都要带着 300 件最珍贵的宝贝去工作，把 DJ 台变成一个充满 50 年历史精美文物的活体快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你最喜欢的播客平台上收听爱彼带来的《重构者》吧。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Sabrina Tavernisi and this is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的萨布丽娜·塔韦尼西，这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In a major new advance in science, DNA from Bronze Age skeletons is providing new clues to modern-day medical mysteries.
sentences.zh: 科学领域的一项重大新进展显示，从青铜时代骨骼中提取的 DNA 正为现代医学谜题提供新的线索。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Carl Zimmer explains how a new field of science is changing the way we think about treatments for devastating diseases.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事卡尔·齐默将解释一个新的科学领域如何改变我们对治疗毁灭性疾病的看法。

sentences.en: It's Wednesday, January 31St.
sentences.zh: 今天是 1 月 31 日，星期三。

sentences.en: So Carl, you are a science reporter, as our listeners will know, and you write about evolution and the origins of life.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，听众们都知道你是一位科学记者，你撰写关于进化和生命起源的文章。

sentences.en: And you've recently written a story that really piqued my intereSt.
sentences.zh: 你最近写的一篇报道确实引起了我的兴趣。

sentences.en: It was about a major new discovery in our understanding of ancient people.
sentences.zh: 那是关于我们对古人类理解的一项重大新发现。

sentences.en: And it's leading to some big advances, as I understand it, in modern medicine.
sentences.zh: 据我所知，这正引领着现代医学的一些重大进步。

sentences.en: So tell me about it.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说吧。

sentences.en: Well, scientists have been wondering about two big questions for a long time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，科学家们长期以来一直对两个大问题感到好奇。

sentences.en: One of them is, why do we get sick?
sentences.zh: 其中之一是：我们为什么会生病？

sentences.en: The other question is, where do we come from?
sentences.zh: 另一个问题是：我们从哪里来？

sentences.en: And they seem like they should have two very different answers.
sentences.zh: 这两个问题看起来应该有两个截然不同的答案。

sentences.en: But now scientists are starting to realize maybe the two questions actually have the same answer.
sentences.zh: 但现在科学家们开始意识到，这两个问题或许有着相同的答案。

sentences.en: The same answer how, Carl?
sentences.zh: 卡尔，怎么会是相同的答案呢？

sentences.en: Well, it's possible that in order to treat the diseases we have to deal with today, diseases often that have no treatment yet,
sentences.zh: 嗯，为了治疗我们今天必须面对的疾病，那些往往还没有治疗方法的疾病，

sentences.en: it may be necessary to go back thousands of years and look at how our ancestors lived then.
sentences.zh: 我们可能有必要回溯几千年，看看我们的祖先当时是如何生活的。

sentences.en: What were the challenges they faced?
sentences.zh: 他们面临着什么样的挑战？

sentences.en: What was their health like?
sentences.zh: 他们的健康状况如何？

sentences.en: What kind of genes did they carry?
sentences.zh: 他们携带什么样的基因？

sentences.en: And maybe we can then come back to the present and start to be able to make our own health better.
sentences.zh: 也许我们能带着这些答案回到现在，开始改善我们自己的健康。

sentences.en: And now researchers have just made some really big discoveries, both about human history and about our diseases at the same time.
sentences.zh: 现在研究人员刚刚在人类历史和我们的疾病方面同时取得了一些重大发现。

sentences.en: And this history actually lives inside of us right now, in our own genes, and has big implications for our health.
sentences.zh: 这段历史实际上就存在于我们当下的基因里，并对我们的健康有着重大影响。

sentences.en: Okay, so two branches of science coming together, as you say, making some major new discoveries.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以正如你所说，两个科学分支正在汇合，并取得了一些重大的新发现。

sentences.en: So tell me about this first field of science, Carl.
sentences.zh: 那么，卡尔，先跟我说说这个科学领域吧。

sentences.en: What's happening there?
sentences.zh: 那里正在发生什么？

sentences.en: Well, you know, once upon a time, if you wanted to study ancient life, you were pretty much limited to fossils.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，曾几何时，如果你想研究古代生命，你基本上只能局限于化石。

sentences.en: You know, after an animal or a person died, their body's decomposed.
sentences.zh: 你知道，动物或人死后，身体就会分解。

sentences.en: And if you're lucky, their bones managed to survive in rock.
sentences.zh: 如果你运气好，它们的骨头能保存在岩石中。

sentences.en: And then thousands or millions of years later, a paleontologist would come along and dig those fossils out.
sentences.zh: 几千或几百万年后，古生物学家会把这些化石挖掘出来。

sentences.en: But now it is actually possible to dig up those bones and to drill a little sample out of them and find some DNA still surviving in it.
sentences.zh: 但现在，我们实际上可以挖掘出这些骨头，钻取一小块样本，并从中找到仍然存活的 DNA。

sentences.en: So this actually gives you a glimpse into, you know, the molecular life of these ancient people or ancient animals.
sentences.zh: 这让你得以一窥这些古人类或古代动物的分子生命。

sentences.en: And it's amazing enough when scientists can get just a single gene out of a fossil that's thousands and thousands of years old.
sentences.zh: 当科学家能从几千年前的化石中提取出哪怕一个基因时，这已经足够令人惊叹了。

sentences.en: But actually, the science has come so far in recent years that it's pretty common for scientists to get a whole genome of an extinct species.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，近年来科学发展如此迅速，科学家获得灭绝物种的完整基因组已经很常见了。

sentences.en: That is, like, every single gene, every stretch of DNA reconstructed pretty accurately.
sentences.zh: 也就是说，每一个基因，每一段 DNA 都被相当准确地重建了出来。

sentences.en: Once you can look at the whole genome of some ancient organism, you are really starting to get the big picture of how that thing lived.
sentences.zh: 一旦你能看到某种古代生物的完整基因组，你就能真正开始全面了解它是如何生活的。

sentences.en: And looking back at our own past, we can actually use this ancient DNA from fossils to figure out some clues about our ancient relatives going back a couple hundred thousand years,
sentences.zh: 回顾我们自己的过去，我们实际上可以利用化石中的古 DNA 来找出关于我们几万年前古老亲属的一些线索，

sentences.en: actually.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And this includes ancient relatives like Neanderthals, for example.
sentences.zh: 这包括像尼安德特人这样的古老亲属。

sentences.en: So now we can actually see an entire genome of Neanderthal.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们实际上可以看到尼安德特人的完整基因组。

sentences.en: But more recently, what's been really spectacular is actually how scientists have been able to focus on the past 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 但更令人惊叹的是，科学家们最近能够专注于过去 1 万年的历史。

sentences.en: And what we're talking about there is that time in history where hunter-gatherers started to domesticate animals and plants and start to farm.
sentences.zh: 我们所谈论的是历史上狩猎采集者开始驯化动植物并开始耕种的时期。

sentences.en: When you started to have the first towns, when you started to have first large-scale societies.
sentences.zh: 那是你开始看到第一批城镇、第一批大规模社会出现的时期。

sentences.en: And we can actually go now and see what the DNA of these people look like.
sentences.zh: 我们现在实际上可以去看看这些人的 DNA 是什么样的。

sentences.en: Actually, we can see thousands of people from this time period.
sentences.zh: 事实上，我们可以看到那个时期成千上万人的 DNA。

sentences.en: Okay, so we're really getting a clearer picture of how groups of ancient peoples came to be and live their lives many, many years ago.
sentences.zh: 好的，所以我们确实对许多年前古人类群体是如何形成并生活的有了更清晰的了解。

sentences.en: But how specific is that picture?
sentences.zh: 但那幅图景有多具体呢？

sentences.en: Like, what does it look like?
sentences.zh: 比如，它看起来是什么样的？

sentences.en: what are some of the things we're learning, Carl?
sentences.zh: 卡尔，我们正在学习哪些东西？

sentences.en: We're learning about all sorts of things about these people's lives by looking at their DNA.
sentences.zh: 通过观察 DNA，我们正在了解这些人生活的方方面面。

sentences.en: I mean, some people today, you know, they can drink milk and be fine with that.
sentences.zh: 我是说，今天有些人喝牛奶没问题，

sentences.en: And some people are lactose intolerant.
sentences.zh: 而有些人则有乳糖不耐受。

sentences.en: Well, we can actually look back at the DNA and say, who was lactose intolerant among ancient farmers 8,000 years ago?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们实际上可以回顾 DNA，说出 8000 年前的古代农民中谁有乳糖不耐受。

sentences.en: We can say that.
sentences.zh: 我们可以做到这一点。

sentences.en: We can start to actually get clues about the color of the skin of people who lived 10,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 我们可以开始获得关于 1 万年前生活的人们皮肤颜色的线索。

sentences.en: We can figure out how societies were organized.
sentences.zh: 我们可以弄清楚社会是如何组织的。

sentences.en: When you come across a burial with several skeletons in it, when they all have jewelry on it, you can actually show genetically if they're related or not.
sentences.zh: 当你发现一个有几具骨架的墓葬，且他们都佩戴着珠宝时，你可以从基因上证明他们是否有亲缘关系。

sentences.en: And that might tell you you're looking at, say, a royal family.
sentences.zh: 这可能会告诉你，你看到的是一个皇室家族。

sentences.en: And on top of that, look at how these different groups of people with certain genetic markers
sentences.zh: 除此之外，看看这些带有特定遗传标记的不同群体是如何

sentences.en: moved around, how they expanded from one place to another, how two populations might interbreed.
sentences.zh: 四处迁徙的，他们如何从一个地方扩展到另一个地方，两个种群如何杂交。

sentences.en: So there's an astonishing amount that you can learn now from ancient DNA.
sentences.zh: 所以现在从古 DNA 中可以学到的东西多得惊人。

sentences.en: So we're basically seeing the stories of different groups of people over time.
sentences.zh: 所以我们基本上是在观察不同群体随时间推移的故事。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's right.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: And there are groups of people that we didn't really know much about before.
sentences.zh: 而且有些群体是我们以前不太了解的。

sentences.en: People who existed thousands of years ago, who now we're realizing were actually really important to the course of history.
sentences.zh: 那些几千年前存在的人，我们现在意识到他们对历史进程其实非常重要。

sentences.en: And one of those was actually a group called the Yamnaya.
sentences.zh: 其中之一就是一个叫“颜那亚”的群体。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Yamnaya.
sentences.zh: 颜那亚。

sentences.en: That is not a group I am familiar with.
sentences.zh: 这不是我熟悉的群体。

sentences.en: Not a household name.
sentences.zh: 不是家喻户晓的名字。

sentences.en: Well, archaeologists have known about the Yamnaya to some extent for decades, but they couldn't really say that much about them.
sentences.zh: 嗯，考古学家几十年来在一定程度上了解颜那亚人，但他们说不出太多关于他们的信息。

sentences.en: What has become clear now is that the Yamnaya were living, you know, maybe 6,000, 5,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 现在清楚的是，颜那亚人生活在大概 6000 或 5000 年前。

sentences.en: They started out as farmers, but they actually gave up farming because they developed this practice of herding cattle and sheep and goats.
sentences.zh: 他们最初是农民，但后来放弃了耕种，因为他们发展出了放牧牛、羊和山羊的习俗。

sentences.en: And they were incredibly successful at this.
sentences.zh: 他们在这一方面极其成功。

sentences.en: And they were among the first horse riders.
sentences.zh: 他们是最早的骑马者之一。

sentences.en: They would use the horses and other livestock to haul wagons.
sentences.zh: 他们会利用马匹和其他牲畜来拉车。

sentences.en: And they would just go across hundreds of thousands of miles of the steppe from the Ukraine all the way over to Central Asia to places like Kazakhstan.
sentences.zh: 他们会横跨从乌克兰一直到中亚（如哈萨克斯坦）数十万英里的草原。

sentences.en: They went from roaming around to exploding across Europe in Asia.
sentences.zh: 他们从四处游荡变成了在欧洲和亚洲迅速扩张。

sentences.en: And when they showed up, they took over.
sentences.zh: 当他们出现时，他们就接管了一切。

sentences.en: And you can see this actually when they arrive in
sentences.zh: 当你看到他们抵达

sentences.en: Denmark, for example.
sentences.zh: 丹麦时，就能发现这一点。

sentences.en: Scientists have looked very closely at the DNA in Denmark from skeletons over the past 10,000 years.
sentences.zh: 科学家们非常仔细地研究了过去 1 万年里丹麦骨骼中的 DNA。

sentences.en: And you can see that there's a group of farmers there with a certain kind of ancestry.
sentences.zh: 你可以看到那里有一群具有某种血统的农民。

sentences.en: And then, boom, the Yamnaya show up about 5,000 years ago.
sentences.zh: 然后，砰，大约 5000 年前，颜那亚人出现了。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: It's all
sentences.zh: 全都是

sentences.en: Yamnaya.
sentences.zh: 颜那亚人。

sentences.en: So they showed up in Northern Europe from Central Asia and at some point became the dominant population.
sentences.zh: 所以他们从中亚来到北欧，并在某个时刻成为了主导人口。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We don't know exactly how that happened.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道这具体是怎么发生的。

sentences.en: There are some very dark possibilities.
sentences.zh: 有一些非常黑暗的可能性。

sentences.en: This could have been some kind of genocide.
sentences.zh: 这可能是一种种族灭绝。

sentences.en: Or maybe it wasn't such a violent transition.
sentences.zh: 或者这种过渡可能没有那么暴力。

sentences.en: Maybe it was a competition for land that took decades to play out.
sentences.zh: 也许是持续了几十年的土地竞争。

sentences.en: But in any case, we know that the Yamnaya became the people of the region.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，我们知道颜那亚人成为了该地区的主人。

sentences.en: And then they became the ancestors of people in Northern Europe today.
sentences.zh: 然后他们成为了今天北欧人的祖先。

sentences.en: People today with Northern European ancestry, they come from the Yamnaya.
sentences.zh: 今天有北欧血统的人，他们来自颜那亚人。

sentences.en: And Carl, why are these people important?
sentences.zh: 卡尔，为什么这些人很重要？

sentences.en: I mean, why are we talking about Yamnaya in the context of this genetic stuff?
sentences.zh: 我是说，为什么我们在这些遗传学背景下谈论颜那亚人？

sentences.en: Well, in addition to being really important to the course of history, they actually matter to us today.
sentences.zh: 嗯，除了对历史进程非常重要之外，他们对我们今天也很重要。

sentences.en: Because locked inside of their DNA 5,000 years ago are some really crucial secrets about some of the most devastating diseases we suffer from today.
sentences.zh: 因为在他们 5000 年前的 DNA 中锁着一些关于我们今天所患最严重疾病的关键秘密。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33 位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 4.30 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨 4 点 30 分给总统打电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60 款超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们可能每年都是联盟里最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝 175 年来帮助你了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受 nytimes.com/subscribe 的特别优惠。

sentences.en: So Carl, you said that this new science was showing us something important about these Yamnaya people and it had to do with disease, this little code locked inside their DNA.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，你说这项新科学向我们展示了关于颜那亚人的重要信息，而且这与疾病有关，即锁在他们 DNA 里的那段小密码。

sentences.en: Tell me about that.
sentences.zh: 跟我说说那个吧。

sentences.en: So this brings us to the second field of science I was talking about, which is the basic question of why we get sick.
sentences.zh: 这把我们带到了我刚才提到的第二个科学领域，也就是关于我们为什么会生病的基本问题。

sentences.en: We get these diseases and they seem to have all sorts of just random symptoMs.
sentences.zh: 我们患上这些疾病，它们似乎有着各种各样的随机症状。

sentences.en: But if you can understand their history, if you can understand their evolution, maybe they're not as random as they seem.
sentences.zh: 但如果你能理解它们的历史，如果你能理解它们的进化，也许它们并不像看起来那么随机。

sentences.en: Maybe by understanding their history, we're going to be able to treat them.
sentences.zh: 也许通过了解它们的历史，我们将能够治疗它们。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So this is these two fields of science coming together like a kind of, you know, scientific chocolate, peanut butter, Reese's peanut butter cup.
sentences.zh: 所以这就是这两个科学领域结合在一起，就像某种科学版的巧克力花生酱，瑞斯花生酱杯。

sentences.en: But what's the process once they come together?
sentences.zh: 但它们结合后的过程是什么样的？

sentences.en: Like how do you study disease in ancient people?
sentences.zh: 比如你如何研究古人的疾病？

sentences.en: So on the one hand, you have some scientists who are looking at the DNA of living people
sentences.zh: 一方面，有些科学家正在观察活人的 DNA，

sentences.en: and finding different variations in their genes that put them at risk for certain diseases.
sentences.zh: 并发现他们基因中导致某些疾病风险的变异。

sentences.en: There are genes that can raise your risk for heart disease, for cancer, for schizophrenia, for all sorts of conditions.
sentences.zh: 有些基因会增加你患心脏病、癌症、精神分裂症等各种疾病的风险。

sentences.en: And scientists have actually been able to create pretty long lists of these genes where there's strong evidence that if you have a certain version of a gene,
sentences.zh: 科学家们实际上已经能够列出这些基因的长名单，有强有力的证据表明，如果你拥有某种版本的基因，

sentences.en: you are at a greater risk of getting these diseases.
sentences.zh: 你患这些疾病的风险就会更高。

sentences.en: And so these scientists who are pulling ancient DNA out of bones that are 5,000, 10,000 years
sentences.zh: 所以这些从 5000 年、1 万年前的骨头中提取古 DNA 的科学家们

sentences.en: old are saying, well, let's see if these people who lived thousands of years ago had those genes too.
sentences.zh: 在说：好吧，让我们看看这些几千年前生活的人是否也有这些基因。

sentences.en: When did these mutations arise and how did they spread?
sentences.zh: 这些突变是什么时候出现的，它们是如何传播的？

sentences.en: Let's trace the whole history of these mutations that today put us at risk of different diseases.
sentences.zh: 让我们追踪这些今天让我们面临不同疾病风险的突变的全部历史。

sentences.en: So how exactly do they do that?
sentences.zh: 那么他们究竟是怎么做到的呢？

sentences.en: Well, one of these projects is based on a British database called the UK Biobank.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其中一个项目基于一个名为“英国生物样本库”的数据库。

sentences.en: What happens there is that half a million volunteers have submitted their DNA and allowed scientists to compare their DNA to their own medical records.
sentences.zh: 那里发生的事情是，50 万名志愿者提交了他们的 DNA，并允许科学家将他们的 DNA 与他们自己的医疗记录进行比较。

sentences.en: And so that they can see links between their genetic variations and the kinds of diseases they're suffering from.
sentences.zh: 这样他们就能看到他们的基因变异与他们所患疾病之间的联系。

sentences.en: So basically, these scientists are tracing the diseases people have to mutations in their genes and looking for patterns across populations.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，这些科学家正在将人们所患的疾病追溯到基因突变，并寻找跨人群的模式。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And so then what you can do is you can compare their DNA of these living people in Britain to all of this ancient DNA from across Europe and Asia.
sentences.zh: 然后你可以做的是，将这些英国活人的 DNA 与来自欧洲和亚洲的所有这些古 DNA 进行比较。

sentences.en: And you can try to figure out, well, where is their DNA coming from?
sentences.zh: 你可以试着弄清楚：好吧，他们的 DNA 是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: Who did they inherit their DNA from?
sentences.zh: 他们从谁那里继承了 DNA？

sentences.en: And did they actually inherit some of these disease genes from those ancient people?
sentences.zh: 他们是否真的从那些古人那里继承了一些疾病基因？

sentences.en: So it's kind of like a 23andMe to figure out who you were related to in the Bronze Age, right?
sentences.zh: 这就像是某种“23andMe”基因检测，用来查明你在青铜时代和谁有亲缘关系，对吧？

sentences.en: And whether they passed down anything to you that might make you sick now.
sentences.zh: 以及他们是否遗传给了你什么可能导致你现在生病的基因。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And what they found were mutations that today we know increase people's risks for a whole bunch of different diseases.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了一些突变，我们现在知道这些突变会增加人们患上一系列不同疾病的风险。

sentences.en: But with a twiSt. Some of these mutations were beneficial to those people thousands of years ago.
sentences.zh: 但有个转折。其中一些突变对几千年前的那些人来说是有益的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That is kind of mind-blowing.
sentences.zh: 这真是令人大开眼界。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So explain that to me, Carl.
sentences.zh: 那么卡尔，给我解释一下。

sentences.en: What's an example?
sentences.zh: 有什么例子吗？

sentences.en: So we can go back to the Yamnaya for a really powerful example of this.
sentences.zh: 我们可以回到颜那亚人（Yamnaya）那里，看看这方面一个非常有力的例子。

sentences.en: So the Yamnaya were herding animals.
sentences.zh: 颜那亚人是游牧民族。

sentences.en: They were with their animals all the time.
sentences.zh: 他们一直和动物待在一起。

sentences.en: They were just going back and forth along the step, always with the animals.
sentences.zh: 他们就在草原上往返奔波，始终与动物为伴。

sentences.en: And that was great because that gave them a source of meat.
sentences.zh: 这很棒，因为这让他们有了肉食来源。

sentences.en: It gave them a source of milk, of leather, wool, like this incredible resource to just have right on hand.
sentences.zh: 这为他们提供了奶、皮革、羊毛，就像是一种随时可用的绝佳资源。

sentences.en: But animals have something else.
sentences.zh: 但动物身上还有别的东西。

sentences.en: They have diseases.
sentences.zh: 它们携带疾病。

sentences.en: And so if you're going to be living with animals, you are actually at risk of picking up some of the diseases that they're carrying.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你要和动物生活在一起，你实际上就有感染它们所携带疾病的风险。

sentences.en: So Carl, were the Yamnaya the first people to actually live with animals and then therefore get sick from them?
sentences.zh: 那么卡尔，颜那亚人是第一批真正与动物共同生活并因此染病的人类吗？

sentences.en: Well, the Yamnaya were getting diseases from animals at a rate that was really different than people had before because they were living with these animals so much of the time.
sentences.zh: 嗯，颜那亚人感染动物疾病的频率与之前的人类确实不同，因为他们大部分时间都和这些动物生活在一起。

sentences.en: And we actually know that because we can see it for ourselves in their bones.
sentences.zh: 我们之所以知道这一点，是因为我们能在他们的骨骼中亲眼看到证据。

sentences.en: When you drill into the bones of the Yamnaya or other ancient people, you can get out the DNA of the people themselves.
sentences.zh: 当你钻入颜那亚人或其他古代人的骨骼时，你可以提取出他们自身的DNA。

sentences.en: And sometimes you can also get the DNA out of the germs that killed them.
sentences.zh: 有时你也能从杀死他们的病菌中提取出DNA。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Amazing.
sentences.zh: 太神奇了。

sentences.en: It is amazing.
sentences.zh: 确实很神奇。

sentences.en: And we know for a fact that they were dealing with a lot of diseases.
sentences.zh: 而且我们确切地知道，他们当时在应对许多疾病。

sentences.en: And it turns out that they were actually evolving a resistance to them.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，他们实际上正在进化出对这些疾病的抵抗力。

sentences.en: Evolving resistance to them?
sentences.zh: 进化出抵抗力？

sentences.en: How exactly?
sentences.zh: 具体是怎么做到的？

sentences.en: So if you had a mutation that ramped up your immune system so that you were better able to fight off
sentences.zh: 如果你有一种突变，能增强你的免疫系统，使你更有能力抵御

sentences.en: these germs that were spilling over from these animals all around you, that would mean you're more likely to live long enough to have kids and pass down that gene to them.
sentences.zh: 那些从你周围动物身上传播过来的病菌，那就意味着你更有可能活得足够长，从而繁衍后代并将该基因遗传给他们。

sentences.en: So if you look across the DNA of Yamnaya, they have a lot of mutations for the first time that are associated with a really strong immune response.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你审视颜那亚人的DNA，会发现他们首次拥有了许多与强效免疫反应相关的突变。

sentences.en: But there's something else that's really important about these genes in the Yamnaya.
sentences.zh: 但关于颜那亚人的这些基因，还有一点非常重要。

sentences.en: These are some of the same genes that today can put people at risk for certain diseases.
sentences.zh: 这些基因中，有一些正是今天可能导致人们患上某些疾病的基因。

sentences.en: And one of those diseases is multiple sclerosis.
sentences.zh: 其中一种疾病就是多发性硬化症。

sentences.en: Multiple sclerosis, like very debilitating disease.
sentences.zh: 多发性硬化症，那是一种非常致残的疾病。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: When people develop multiple sclerosis, their immune cells look at their own nerves as the enemy.
sentences.zh: 当人们患上多发性硬化症时，他们的免疫细胞会将自身的神经视为敌人。

sentences.en: They actually will attack the nerves in the body.
sentences.zh: 它们实际上会攻击体内的神经。

sentences.en: And this is incredibly debilitating.
sentences.zh: 这极其令人虚弱。

sentences.en: It can progress to the point where people can't walk, have trouble talking.
sentences.zh: 它会恶化到人们无法行走、说话困难的地步。

sentences.en: You know, it affects millions of people today.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它今天影响着数百万人。

sentences.en: And yet we're seeing some of the genes that put people at risk of
sentences.zh: 然而，我们却看到一些导致人们今天患上

sentences.en: MS today actually being beneficial in the Yamnaya.
sentences.zh: 多发性硬化症风险的基因，在颜那亚人身上实际上是有益的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So explain that, Carl.
sentences.zh: 那么卡尔，解释一下。

sentences.en: Like how was it protective to the Yamnaya, but obviously very debilitating and problematic today?
sentences.zh: 为什么它对颜那亚人有保护作用，但在今天却显然非常致残且麻烦？

sentences.en: Like how did that happen?
sentences.zh: 这是怎么发生的？

sentences.en: So if we go back to the Yamnaya, four or 5,000 years ago, they are being exposed to a lot of diseases, a lot of bacteria, maybe a lot of viruses.
sentences.zh: 如果我们回到四五千年前的颜那亚时代，他们当时暴露在许多疾病、许多细菌，或许还有许多病毒之中。

sentences.en: Now, recently, like in the past century, a lot of those pathogens have gone away.
sentences.zh: 现在，比如在过去的一个世纪里，许多那样的病原体已经消失了。

sentences.en: So you have pasteurized milk, you have clean water, you have all these innovations that make these pathogens much less of a threat to people's health.
sentences.zh: 所以你有巴氏消毒奶，有干净的水，有所有这些让病原体对人类健康威胁大大降低的创新。

sentences.en: But they still have this aggressive immune system.
sentences.zh: 但他们仍然拥有这种激进的免疫系统。

sentences.en: They still have an immune system that evolved for this tug of war with the pathogens.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然拥有一个为与病原体进行“拔河”而进化的免疫系统。

sentences.en: And now, if the immune system is not being continually challenged by these pathogens, it looks like sometimes the immune system makes mistakes.
sentences.zh: 而现在，如果免疫系统不再持续受到这些病原体的挑战，看起来有时免疫系统就会犯错。

sentences.en: In its aggressiveness, it misfires.
sentences.zh: 由于其攻击性，它会误伤。

sentences.en: So that there are opportunities to get confused and to start to look at a person's own body as the enemy.
sentences.zh: 因此，它就有可能产生混淆，开始将一个人自身的身体视为敌人。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That's pretty interesting that like something that was so protective through the ages suddenly
sentences.zh: 这非常有趣，某种在漫长岁月中如此具有保护性的东西，突然间

sentences.en: becomes a real hindrance because everything changed really in the past hundred years or so.
sentences.zh: 变成了一种真正的阻碍，因为在过去一百年左右的时间里，一切都变了。

sentences.en: But how exactly does knowing this actually help people who have MS today, Carl?
sentences.zh: 但卡尔，了解这一点究竟如何帮助今天患有多发性硬化症的人呢？

sentences.en: What are the practical implications here?
sentences.zh: 这有什么实际意义吗？

sentences.en: Well, it helps us to understand why it is that some people get MS and other people don't.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它帮助我们理解为什么有些人会患上多发性硬化症，而另一些人不会。

sentences.en: Recent research has pointed to a virus called Epstein-Barr as the trigger for Ms. In other words, you probably don't get MS unless you get infected with Epstein-Barr.
sentences.zh: 最近的研究指出，一种名为EB病毒（Epstein-Barr）的病毒是多发性硬化症的诱因。换句话说，如果你没有感染EB病毒，你可能就不会患上多发性硬化症。

sentences.en: But the fact is that most people get infected with Epstein-Barr and maybe a couple million people have Ms. So clearly there's something special about these people.
sentences.zh: 但事实是，大多数人都感染过EB病毒，而可能只有几百万人患有多发性硬化症。所以显然，这些人身上有些特殊之处。

sentences.en: And what's special is that they have inherited these genes.
sentences.zh: 而特殊之处就在于他们遗传了这些基因。

sentences.en: And if you can understand how those genes first evolved, what their functions were for 5,000 years ago, that can actually help you to understand how they're going wrong now.
sentences.zh: 如果你能理解这些基因最初是如何进化的，它们在五千年前的功能是什么，那实际上就能帮助你理解它们现在是如何出错的。

sentences.en: So, you know, right now there are some, you know, fairly effective treatments for Ms. They're okay for some people.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，目前有一些相当有效的多发性硬化症治疗方法。对某些人来说还可以。

sentences.en: They're not great for others, but they're crude.
sentences.zh: 对其他人来说效果不佳，而且它们很粗糙。

sentences.en: They're kind of like a sledgehammer.
sentences.zh: 它们就像一把大锤。

sentences.en: Basically, they just sort of take the immune system and just dial it all down.
sentences.zh: 基本上，它们只是把免疫系统调低了。

sentences.en: That's good in some ways because then your immune system is not going to be attacking yourself so readily.
sentences.zh: 这在某些方面是好事，因为这样你的免疫系统就不会那么轻易地攻击你自己了。

sentences.en: But, you know, like you do need your immune system.
sentences.zh: 但是，你知道，你确实需要你的免疫系统。

sentences.en: You actually do need it to avoid getting really sick from infections.
sentences.zh: 你确实需要它来避免因感染而病得很重。

sentences.en: So really what we need to do is find a better balance.
sentences.zh: 所以我们真正需要做的是找到更好的平衡。

sentences.en: We need to understand that what's happening is that the immune system just has lost this partner in this dance of survival.
sentences.zh: 我们需要明白，现在发生的情况是，免疫系统在这场生存之舞中失去了舞伴。

sentences.en: And so how can we mimic that?
sentences.zh: 那么我们该如何模仿那种平衡呢？

sentences.en: Are there drugs that could actually, like, give the immune system that balance again without us having to get really sick and things like that?
sentences.zh: 有没有什么药物可以真正让免疫系统重新获得那种平衡，而不需要我们病得很重之类的？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So understanding the origins means we go from treating MS with this big sledgehammer to a little scalpel, right?
sentences.zh: 所以理解起源意味着我们从用大锤治疗多发性硬化症，转变为使用精细的手术刀，对吧？

sentences.en: We can really fine-tune the treatment.
sentences.zh: 我们可以真正微调治疗方案。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And we start to understand, you know, why different people are at greater risk of getting Ms. You know, why are the rates highest in Northern Europe?
sentences.zh: 我们开始理解为什么不同的人患多发性硬化症的风险更高。你知道，为什么北欧的发病率最高？

sentences.en: You know, people came up with all sorts of stories for a long time, but we actually know why.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们长期以来编造了各种各样的故事，但我们实际上知道原因。

sentences.en: We know because the Yamnaya showed up.
sentences.zh: 我们知道是因为颜那亚人出现了。

sentences.en: So it takes some of the randomness out of it, right?
sentences.zh: 所以这消除了一些随机性，对吧？

sentences.en: This research has really helped us understand something incredibly important about this very debilitating disease.
sentences.zh: 这项研究确实帮助我们理解了关于这种极度致残疾病的一些极其重要的事情。

sentences.en: It has.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And this is really just a trial run for this whole approach.
sentences.zh: 而这实际上只是这种方法的一次试运行。

sentences.en: This research was based just on the UK Biopank, just on people in Britain.
sentences.zh: 这项研究仅仅基于英国生物样本库（UK Biobank），仅仅基于英国人。

sentences.en: But when we look forward, it's not just going to be
sentences.zh: 但当我们展望未来时，科学家们要解析的将不仅仅是

sentences.en: British people whose history scientists are going to be unpacking.
sentences.zh: 英国人的历史。

sentences.en: It's going to be people all over the world.
sentences.zh: 它将是全世界人民的历史。

sentences.en: We're going to be learning not just about multiple sclerosis, but we're going to be learning about diseases like heart disease, diabetes, conditions like schizophrenia.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅将了解多发性硬化症，还将了解心脏病、糖尿病、精神分裂症等疾病。

sentences.en: And it may be possible to understand how it is that actually maybe the genes that put us at risk of these diseases today were giving us other benefits thousands of years ago.
sentences.zh: 而且我们或许有可能理解，为什么今天让我们面临这些疾病风险的基因，在几千年前可能曾给我们带来其他益处。

sentences.en: So in effect, we could be sitting on a whole new cache of future cures, right, in all of our archaeological sites.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，我们可能正坐拥着一个全新的未来疗法宝库，对吧，就在我们所有的考古遗址中。

sentences.en: Like, is the future of medical research paleontology?
sentences.zh: 医学研究的未来是古生物学吗？

sentences.en: It could be.
sentences.zh: 有可能是。

sentences.en: It could be.
sentences.zh: 有可能是。

sentences.en: This is what scientists sometimes call evolutionary medicine.
sentences.zh: 这就是科学家有时所说的进化医学。

sentences.en: But really, up till now, it's been more of an idea than a reality.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，到目前为止，它更多是一个想法而非现实。

sentences.en: But the experts I talk to say that with ancient DNA research like this, evolutionary medicine is now finally coming of age.
sentences.zh: 但我交谈过的专家表示，有了这样的古代DNA研究，进化医学终于成熟了。

sentences.en: Carl, thank you.
sentences.zh: 卡尔，谢谢你。

sentences.en: Thanks so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是Wena Liu。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我编写了《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我还喜欢尝试捉弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是Sam Mazursky，我每天负责制作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”（promesthesia）的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由人制作的，就像你刚才听到的那些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问nytimes.com/games，今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you should know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还应该知道的消息。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, in a partisan indictment of President Biden's border policy,
sentences.zh: 周二，在针对拜登总统边境政策的一次党派色彩浓厚的弹劾中，

sentences.en: House Republicans began pushing through articles of impeachment against Homeland Security Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas.
sentences.zh: 众议院共和党人开始推动针对国土安全部长亚历杭德罗·马约卡斯的弹劾条款。

sentences.en: Republicans are poised to charge Mayorkas with refusing to uphold the law and with breaching the public trust in his handling of a surge of migrants across the U.S.
sentences.zh: 共和党人准备指控马约卡斯拒绝维护法律，并在处理美国与墨西哥边境移民激增问题上违背公众信任。

sentences.en: border with Mexico.
sentences.zh: 边境。

sentences.en: Democrats and many legal scholars say the committee has not produced any evidence that the secretary has committed an impeachable offense.
sentences.zh: 民主党人和许多法律学者表示，委员会没有提供任何证据表明部长犯下了可弹劾的罪行。

sentences.en: Even if the House votes to impeach Mayorkas, he is not likely to be convicted or removed by the Democratic-controlled Senate.
sentences.zh: 即使众议院投票弹劾马约卡斯，他也不太可能在民主党控制的参议院被定罪或罢免。

sentences.en: But the action could force an election-year trial on the politically charged issue of immigration and the southern border.
sentences.zh: 但此举可能会在选举年强行就移民和南部边境这一政治敏感议题进行审判。

sentences.en: And Hamas said it was considering a proposal to pause the fighting in Gaza and exchange Israeli hostages for Palestinian prisoners.
sentences.zh: 哈马斯表示，正在考虑一项暂停加沙战斗并以以色列人质交换巴勒斯坦囚犯的提议。

sentences.en: The deal's terms were finalized in Paris over the weekend by the United States, Qatar, Egypt and Israel
sentences.zh: 该协议的条款是周末在巴黎由美国、卡塔尔、埃及和以色列敲定的，

sentences.en: and involves a six-week ceasefire in exchange for the release of more hostages.
sentences.zh: 涉及为换取更多人质获释而进行为期六周的停火。
